Dated : 15-07-2024  Shri Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner.
 Shri Sohit Mishra, learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State.

2. Earlier the petitioner being aggrieved by the construction of the road over his agricultural land situated at by-pass road from A.B. Road, Morena to Ambah, had preferred a writ petition No.2182/1996 but the same was dismissed for want of prosecution on 26.10.1998.
3. After the dismissal of the aforesaid writ petition the petitioner preferred an MCC No.525/2005 for its restoration.

The said MCC was dismissed vide order dated 25.11.2005 holding that in the application for condonation of delay in preferring the MCC at a belated stage, no cogent reason was assigned for condoning the delay of seven years.
4. Further in the order, it was observed by this Court that the applicant shall be free to file a fresh writ petition.
Consequently the present petition came 2 WP-3372-2006 to be filed.

In para 04 of the present writ petition which pertains to delay in filing the petition, it is mentioned by the petitioner as under:-

sentences.text:
4. Delay, if any, in filing Petition:
The earlier petition No. 2182/1996 has been dismissed by this Hon'ble Court due to non appearance of the petitioner's counsel Shri Ashok Velankar, Advocate on 26.10.1998.

The petitioner filed MCC No. 525/2005 before this Hon'ble Court for restoration of the above petition, the same was decided on 25.11.2005 and it has been decided by this Hon'ble Court on 25.11.2005 with liberty to file a fresh petition.
According to the above circumstances in the case, the petitioner is unaware from the facts that the petition has been dismissed due to non appearance of petitioner's counsel.
Whenever, petitioner asked his counsel Shri Velankar, Advocate regarding the progress of the petition, he always told that petition is pending and the reply of the state government is awaited.
In these circumstances there is no delay in filing the present petition.

5. After perusing the order passed in MCC No.525/2005 dated 25.11.2005 it is seen that the explanation which was afforded by the present petitioner for delay in preferring the MCC, same explanation has been given in the present petition for condoning the delay and from the order passed in MCC, it could be seen that no liberty as such was granted to the petitioner to prefer a fresh petition, rather it was observed that the petitioner was free to prefer writ petition and, therefore, the law of limitation would be fully applicable in the present case.
6. By way of the present petition relief of compensation towards loss caused to the petitioner due to the taking over of his land in the year 1996 has been sought.

The loss @ 10,000/- per year since 1996 has been quantified on the basis that the crops,
which were standing over the lands have been destroyed and in future the petitioner would be deprived of from the said income to the extent of the aforesaid amount,
therefore, he may be awarded compensation.

So far as the land in lieu of the land which has been taken over 3 WP-3372-2006 by the State is not in dispute as in exchange 02 bighas of land bearing survey No.1108 had already been allotted to the petitioner.

7. Further from the relief, which has been sought, it is seen that prayer has been made to free the land belonging to the petitioner from the encroachment and even the part of the Bye-pass road,
which had crossed over and had been constructed on the land be removed and the land be made usable for agricultural purpose.
Further, a direction has been sought to register a criminal case under Section 420, 467, 468 of IPC against the respondent No.2 for passing forged and fabricated order in regard to the encroachment.
8. For the relief which has been claimed as aforesaid, the remedy to the petitioner lay elsewhere but instead of availing those legal remedies he has chosen to prefer writ petition.

This Court on 08.01.2024 had observed that prima facie it appears that petition is not maintainable, however, in the interest of justice time was granted to the petitioner to address upon the maintainability of the Dr.Munshiram Dandotia vs State Of M.P. on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13488530/
2 petition.
9.

sentences.text: Today, counsel for the petitioner could not raise any argument before this Court with regard to the maintainability of the writ petition, rather he had argued the matter on merits, which according to this Court cannot be gone into as the relief which has been claimed by the petitioner cannot be entertained under the writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
10. Under the aforesaid observation, the present petition stands dismissed.
